title: Penguin Analysis (Bill Length)
text:
Figure 1 is shown below and shows the varying bill lengths in millimeters for different penguin species grouped by sex. From the chart below, while male penguins mostly have longer bills compared to female penguins, the female penguins of the Chinstrap species display the opposite behavior.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

modified_penguins <- penguins
modified_penguins <- drop_na(modified_penguins, sex)
modified_penguins <- ggplot(data = modified_penguins, mapping = aes  (x = species,
    y = bill_length_mm,
    fill = sex)) +
    geom_col(position='dodge') +
    xlab("Species") +
    ylab("Bill Length (mm)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 18))
modified_penguins








Figure 1: Bill length of penguins by species.





Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

title: Edmund Yong
text: My name is Edmund Yong and I am part of the UBC MDS 2027 cohort. I am from Tennessee in the United States and I studied at East Tennessee State University for my undergraduate degree in Computer Science. Before MDS, I worked at CGI for 4 years as a Software Engineer Consultant, creating software solutions for various clients and companies in Nashville, TN. During my time at CGI, I gained exposure to data engineering and data science. My hope with this program is to expand on what I learned about data science while working for numerous clients.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
While getting my bachelor’s degree in computer science, I had the opportunity to write an undergraduate thesiswhich involved training a model to play Cassino, a lesser-known card game that my thesis mentor had played as a child. My research led me to learn about different machine learning methods that could train agents to play both deterministic and non-deterministic games. Although the model I trained to play Cassino performed very poorly, the knowledge and experience I gained from my thesis are what sparked my interest in data science.

title: About
text:
Outside of Data Science
Outside of data science, my hobbies can range anywhere from video games, learning languages, scuba diving, badminton, and many other activities. Outside of these, I’m always open to trying new activities.
